title: Linkability of Student Identity to Submission Data
description: The flow transmits student id, course, and submission timestamp alongside the work file, enabling potential linking of the student's identity to their academic submission data.
assumptions: The system stores and processes this data in a way that allows correlation between student identity and submission content.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability threats at the source position.

title: Identification of Student Through Login Credentials
description: The student must authenticate to submit assignments, which inherently identifies them to the system and potentially to other system components.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are in place and the system processes the student's identity information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identification threats at the source position.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Submission Data
description: The work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the Grades Portal Web App or insecure data transmission.
assumptions: The system has access controls and the data is transmitted over secure channels.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for disclosure threats at the source position.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity for Assignment Submission
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a student to submit assignments on their behalf, either through credential theft or system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft or bypass.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for usurpation threats at the source position.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This flow inherently contains unique references to student identity, creating an identifier threat at the source of transmission.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats; confidence in mapping to this specific flow is moderate.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This constitutes processing of identified data as defined in threat tree node I.1.1.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading purposes without additional anonymization or pseudonymization.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data; confidence in mapping to this specific flow is moderate.

title: Non-repudiation of Grading Actions
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes grading requests and submissions, creating evidence that could prevent individuals from denying their involvement in grading decisions or submission actions. This non-repudiation threat arises from the permanent record of who submitted what and when.
assumptions: Grading actions and submissions are logged with sufficient detail to prevent denial of involvement.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation context [4] indicates this is a threat (inability to deny), not a security goal. Confidence in Nr.1.1 node selection is based on general LINDDUN knowledge.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure of Student Assignment Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) explicitly transfers student assignment files containing student ID, course, and submission time to the Assignment Store (DS1). This is an intentional disclosure by design, which may violate the minimality principle if the stored data exceeds what is strictly necessary for grading purposes.
assumptions: The system stores more personal data than minimally required for the grading function
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context about data disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Implicit Data Disclosure via Stored Assignment Metadata
description: The Assignment Store (DS1) may enable implicit disclosure of student information through metadata (submission time, course association) that could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used to infer additional information about students.
assumptions: Stored metadata can be accessed or correlated with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.2 is inferred; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student personal information (names, work content, submission times) displayed to teacher could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties if teacher account is compromised or if teacher shares data inappropriately with colleagues or students.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for disclosure threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows based on context [3][4].

title: Unauthorized access to student submission data
description: Student submission data could be accessed by unauthorized individuals if the teacher's credentials are compromised, if there are insufficient access controls on the portal, or if the teacher's device is insecure.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for usurpation threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows based on context [3][4].

title: Non-compliance with student data privacy regulations
description: Sharing student personal information with teachers must comply with FERPA/GDPR regulations. Inappropriate sharing, lack of proper consent, or failure to implement required safeguards could result in regulatory violations.
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for non-compliance threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows based on context [3][4].

title: Student data linkability across system flows
description: Student identifiers recorded in this flow could be linked to other student data flows (e.g., enrollment, attendance, other grades), creating a comprehensive student profile that exceeds the scope of this specific grade recording interaction.
assumptions: The system contains multiple data flows involving student identifiers that could be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree node may vary based on full threat tree structure.

title: Student and grader identification through recorded data
description: The student id and grader id fields directly identify individuals. Student identities are exposed through grade records, and teacher identities are exposed through grader id fields, potentially enabling unauthorized identification of students and teachers.
assumptions: Student and teacher identities are not adequately anonymized or pseudonymized in the system.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a general identification node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree node may vary based on full threat tree structure.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and written feedback
description: Written feedback text and grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, parents without proper authorization, or external actors) through the grades portal, potentially violating student privacy and academic integrity.
assumptions: Access controls on the grades portal may not properly restrict who can view grades and feedback.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree node may vary based on full threat tree structure.

title: Teacher identity usurpation for grade recording
description: An unauthorized actor could potentially impersonate a teacher to record grades and feedback, leading to falsified academic records. This is enabled if teacher authentication is weak or if teacher accounts are compromised.
assumptions: Teacher authentication mechanisms may not be sufficiently robust to prevent identity usurpation.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific LINDDUN Pro tree node may vary based on full threat tree structure.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grading service writing to the Grade Records Database could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive student grades and personal information.
assumptions: Database access controls are not properly implemented or are bypassed.

title: Student and Grader Identification
description: The grade records contain student id and grader id, which could be used to identify specific individuals and their academic performance.
assumptions: Student and grader IDs are not properly anonymized or masked.

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (e.g., enrollment records, personal information) to create comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple systems without proper isolation.

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Unauthorized modification of grade records could alter student grades, feedback, or grader information, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Write access controls are insufficient to prevent unauthorized modifications.

title: Data Store Exposure
description: The Grade Records Database itself could be accessed by unauthorized entities, exposing all stored grade records.
assumptions: Database security measures are inadequate or misconfigured.

title: Processing of identified student grades data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified student grades and feedback data, which are personal identifiable information. This processing creates a privacy risk as the data is directly linked to the student's identity.
assumptions: Student grades are considered identified personal data under privacy regulations

title: Linkability of student grades across systems
description: Student grades could be linked to the student's identity across different systems or databases, potentially enabling profiling or unauthorized correlation of data.
assumptions: Grades data may be shared or accessed by multiple systems

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper data handling.
assumptions: Access controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access

title: Student identity usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the student to access their grades and feedback, or the student could be tricked into revealing credentials.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft or social engineering

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades and feedback
description: Student grades and teacher feedback are sensitive personal data. During transmission from the portal to the student, or if intercepted, unauthorized parties could access this information. The flow involves displaying personal academic data that could be exposed through network vulnerabilities, insecure endpoints, or compromised credentials.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may have vulnerabilities in data transmission or storage, and that unauthorized access could occur.

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: The student's grades and feedback displayed in this flow could be linked with other data sources (e.g., enrollment records, behavioral data, other academic systems) to create a comprehensive profile of the student. This linkability could enable tracking of the student across different contexts and services.
assumptions: Assumes the student's identity is consistent across systems and that data could be correlated.

title: Identification of student through grade data
description: The grades and feedback are inherently tied to a specific student, making identification possible. If the data is exposed or accessed by unauthorized parties, the student could be identified even if other identifiers are removed, as grade patterns and feedback content are unique to the individual.
assumptions: Assumes the grade data contains identifiable information or patterns that could be used to identify the student.

title: Parent Account Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent by compromising their login credentials, gaining unauthorized access to another parent's child grades.
assumptions: Weak authentication or credential theft is possible

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Child grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the system lacks proper access controls or if data is transmitted insecurely.
assumptions: Inadequate access control or insecure data transmission

title: Parent-Child Identity Linking
description: The system may link parent identity to child grades in ways that could be exploited for profiling or tracking across multiple children.
assumptions: System maintains parent-child relationship data that could be correlated

title: Excessive Grade Data Collection
description: The Grades Portal may collect more grade data than necessary (e.g., all subjects, all years) when only specific grades are requested.
assumptions: System retrieves full grade history rather than requested subset

title: Administrator actions linked to parent-child relationships
description: School Administrator (EE4) creates/modifies parent-child links, potentially linking children to their parents through the Grades Portal. This linkability could enable inference of additional sensitive information about family relationships.
assumptions: Administrator has access to create parent-child relationships that can be traced back to the administrator's actions.

title: Administrator identification through account management
description: Administrator (EE4) manages accounts with names, emails, and roles. This identification data could be used to identify specific individuals, potentially leading to unauthorized profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Administrator has access to personal identification data including names and emails.

title: Administrator account usurpation
description: School Administrator (EE4) has elevated privileges to create, modify, and disable accounts. If administrator credentials are compromised or impersonated, unauthorized changes to parent-child relationships and account data could occur.
assumptions: Administrator credentials are protected but could be compromised through phishing, credential theft, or social engineering.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent-child relationships
description: Administrator (EE4) has access to sensitive parent-child relationship data. Improper access controls or logging could lead to unauthorized disclosure of family relationship information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator has access to sensitive relationship data that could be disclosed through improper access controls or logging mechanisms.

title: Identification of Students and Family Members via Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. This could allow identification of students and their family members through the stored relationship data, potentially exposing sensitive family structure information.
assumptions: Account records contain identifiable information about students and their family relationships

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records During Write Operation
description: When the grading service writes account records to the account directory, there is a risk that sensitive student and family information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data exposure during the write process.
assumptions: Write operations to the account directory are not adequately protected

title: Unauthorized Modification of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory. There is a risk that these records could be modified by unauthorized actors, potentially altering student-family relationships or account information.
assumptions: Write operations to the account directory are not adequately protected against modification

title: Linkability of Account Records Across Systems
description: The account directory stores account records with parent-child relationship links. This data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., academic records, financial data) to create comprehensive profiles of students and their families, potentially enabling tracking across different contexts.
assumptions: The account directory data can be correlated with other data sources

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: Third-party provider has access to all PII; data transfer is intentional and by design

title: Identifiability of Students via Grade Records and Account Directory
description: Grade records and account directory contain personally identifiable information that can identify individual students/users. Transfer to third-party increases identifiability risk.
assumptions: Grade records and account directory contain sufficient PII to identify individuals

title: Linkability of Disclosed Data Across Systems
description: Grade records, assignments, and account directory can be linked to identify individuals and potentially correlate with other data sources held by the cloud provider or third parties.
assumptions: Data elements can be cross-referenced to create comprehensive profiles

title: Potential Over-collection of Personal Data (Minimality Violation)
description: Transfer of 'full' grade records, assignments, and account directory may violate minimality principle if not all data elements are strictly necessary for cloud hosting replication purposes.
assumptions: Full data transfer may exceed what's needed for backup/replication
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether 'full' records are necessary or if selective transfer could suffice

title: Third-Party Data Transfer Compliance Risk
description: Transferring personal data to external cloud hosting provider may violate data protection regulations (GDPR, FERPA, etc.) if proper safeguards, contracts, and compliance measures are not in place.
assumptions: Data protection laws apply to this data transfer; third-party may not have adequate compliance measures
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific compliance requirements

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized parties or systems without proper authentication and authorization controls, leading to exposure of sensitive student performance data.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced on the grade records database.

title: Student Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific students, potentially leading to privacy violations if accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Grade records include student identifiers or can be correlated with other data to identify individuals.

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Data
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (e.g., demographic, behavioral) to create comprehensive profiles, potentially revealing more than intended.
assumptions: Grade records can be correlated with other data sources held by the organization.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Sensitive Data
description: Grade records may contain sensitive personal data subject to privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR), and improper handling could result in regulatory violations.
assumptions: Grade records are classified as sensitive personal data under applicable privacy regulations.
